adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 28/12/2016
adventures-mountains.description: This is again the Dent Blanche Peak. Picture taken at the end of the day during the “golden hours”. The picture is taken from the Ferpècle area that is currently one of my favourite hiking spots. It is easily accessible with children and is not too difficult to get to. It is also not very well known and remains somewhat recluse with not that many visitors. From that area, one can see the Dent Blanche but also the Mont Miné Glacier and several other alpine features.

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 21/01/2017
adventures-mountains.description: This is around St Cergues on the Jura. As explained previously in another picture, low hanging clouds or fog often hover over Lake Geneva during the winter making for very grey days. This can go on for several weeks at a time preventing inhabitants down in the plain of getting any sun at all. These clouds are usually under 1’000 meters of altitude and it is quite easy to get above them by going to the Jura or Salève or any place higher up in the Alps. And breaching the clouds can afford some splendid views at times. I took this picture on my birthday. I was tired of being under this iron cover of grey clouds during the winter and thought I should go up and fetch the sun. The feeling when breaching these clouds is just wonderful. One transitions from dark grey winter days into majestic crisp sunny mountain air within just a few miles. And being above the cover contemplating the sea of clouds feels like a little bit of paradise, leaving earth for the skies. Was a great birthday!

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 22/04/2017
adventures-mountains.description: This is above Evolène in the Val d’Hérens at the Lac d’Arbey. I hiked there with a friend on a beautiful summer day. And this friend in question has been living on the African continent for the past decade and it is always fun times to walk and talk with him. Always interesting to be discussing African jungle politics while hiking in the Swiss Alps.

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 31/07/2017
adventures-mountains.description: This is the Vallon de Réchy. I hiked up there from l’Alpage de Loveignoz with my wife. I remember it as a pretty difficult hike, it was a very steep ascent, and I was hauling all my photography gear. But I am quite happy with the view we had up there and of the pictures I took. So much that I made this picture the home page of the website!

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 14/07/2010
adventures-mountains.description: This is the Rhône Glacier. The source of the Rhône river that feeds Lake Geneva, runs through France and ends up in the Mediterranean Sea. There is a beautiful Ice exposition and one can go into the glacier.\n But alas, due to global warming, the glacier is melting quickly, and people have tried to cover up the exposition part with white tarps to slow down the melting. I do not now today in 2020 as I write these lines if the exposition is still accessible or not.

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 06/04/2010
adventures-mountains.description: This is the famous Aletsch Glacier. This picture is taken from a famous tourist spot. There are thousands of the exact same picture all over internet. It is not a super picture, granted, contrasts and colours are a bit off, but still, I had to put it in this collection about mountains.

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 13/12/2007
adventures-mountains.description: This is around St Cergues on the Jura. Low hanging clouds or fog often hover over Lake Geneva during the winter making for very grey days. This can go on for several weeks at a time preventing inhabitants down in the plain of getting any sun at all. These clouds are usually under 1’000 meters of altitude and it is quite easy to get above them by going to the Jura or Salève or any place higher up in the Alps. And breaching the clouds can afford some splendid views at times. On this picture, there are two levels of clouds and I am sandwiched between them but can clearly see the Alps on the other side of the lake (that is under the clouds).

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 07/05/2008
adventures-mountains.description: This is during my army days! Military service in Switzerland is mandatory and every male citizen must go through boot camp (4-6 months) and then go to rehearsal course every year for 3 weeks. This picture was taken during on of these rehearsal course. I was stationed at Flüelen in Canton Uri and had managed to make a deal with the company captain. As I was somewhat on the older side (I was 30 and service lasted until 32 years of age) and wasn’t super motivated to hang out with the 20-year-old kids and do all the drills and practices, I did mostly night watches. So I would stay up all night in my guard shack while the others slept, then would sleep myself in the mornings while the company went out for the day, and would go on these glorious hikes by myself in the afternoons. Was quite enjoyable I must say.

adventures-mountains.title: Georgia - 15/12/2014
adventures-mountains.description: As I live n Switzerland, almost all the mountain pictures I have taken are of the Swiss Alps. With age, I am growing more and more found of mountains (and less of beaches) and might travel to some other mountain ranges and take more pictures. I put this lone picture of a mountain village in Georgia in here just to try to offer a tiny bit of balance to the collection. While I do have many pictures from around the world in other sections, the “Mountains” section tends to be very Switzerland oriented! This picture is taken near Gudauri in Georgia. It might be the village of Kvesheti but I am not sure anymore. Georgia is a beautiful country that could be Switzerland’s Sister (or Brother) country. It is about the same size, also has long standing rural traditions, crazy mountain ranges (but notably higher than the Alps), and beautiful secular cities.

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 25/02/2005
adventures-mountains.description: An older picture taken with a first generation Minolta Digital Camera. I took this before I got interested into photography and bought DSLR gear. I was snowboarding with some friends in a ski resort (Les Diablerets) and took a couple pictures. This is one of a frozen top near where the ski lift drops skiers.

adventures-mountains.title: Switzerland - 18/08/2004
adventures-mountains.description:
This picture was taken somewhere around the Saint Bernard Pass. I was hiking up there with a dear friend of mine and some of his family members.

 We camped on top the mountain near this little lake. I remember the outing as quite fun because we were young and very energetic and had actually brought a whole Fondue Set with us with the wine and the cheese (full load of several kgs) in our backpacks! Full camping gear plus the Fondue set! We had a blast.

orange.title: Ethiopia - 07/01/2016
orange.description: The Danakil Salt Lake at Sunset at the beginning of Lake Karoum. I was working with UNICEF in Ethiopia and took a 4-day week-end with colleagues during the Orthodox Christmas. We toured the Danakil depression which brought us to this salt lake, to the Dallol sulphur pools and to the Erta Ale volcano. Absolute dreamland for a photographer. And on the lucky side, the husband of one of my colleagues was a very well prepared and seasoned adventurer and had his own pimped out 4x4 truck. We went to this salt lake at the start of our trip, it was our first stop, we get out of the cars and start enjoying the beauty of the site when this guy comes over to me while I am taking pictures and hands me a cold beer! The guy had a fridge in his truck and tons of beers! So we are out there in the blistering heat of the Danakil depression drinking cold ones on our camping chairs and just enjoying the sunset. The definition of luxury if you ask me! He also had all kind of European delicacies such as red wine, sausage, ham, etc. So same for the Sulphur pools and the volcano. I had myself just landed back in Ethiopia after a European holiday but the airline had temporarily “misplaced” my luggage. So I went on that tour without my contact lenses (but with crappy old glasses), with a bad pair of shoes not suited for volcano climbing, with only one pair of pants and a t-shirt, etc. and had minimal comfort with me. So this little addition was quite welcome and helped make this trip absolutely memorable.
